_comment: Public-records statutes by state. response_days/business describe the initial response deadline the engine uses to compute due dates and flag overdue requests. Deadlines change — ALWAYS verify against current law before relying on them. Not legal advice. Missing states fall back to a [VERIFY] placeholder so a wrong citation is never silently inserted.

US.name: Freedom of Information Act
US.note: Federal agencies only. Local/state records use the state law.

CA.name: California Public Records Act
CA.note: Determination within 10 days (§ 7922.535); extendable up to 14 days in unusual circumstances.

CO.name: Colorado Open Records Act (CORA)
CO.note: 3 working days, extendable by up to 7 working days in extenuating circumstances.

FL.name: Florida Public Records Law
FL.note: No fixed deadline; custodian must respond promptly and in good faith.

ID.name: Idaho Public Records Act
ID.note: May be extended to 10 working days with notice.

IL.name: Illinois Freedom of Information Act
IL.note: Extendable by 5 business days with written notice (5 ILCS 140/3(e)).

IN.name: Indiana Access to Public Records Act
IN.note: 7 days for mailed/emailed requests; 24 hours in person.

MT.name: Montana Constitution right to know / Public Records
MT.cite: Mont. Const. art. II, § 9; Mont. Code Ann. § 2-6-1001 et seq.

NY.name: Freedom of Information Law (FOIL)
NY.note: Acknowledgement within 5 business days with an approximate date for response.

OR.name: Oregon Public Records Law
OR.note: Acknowledge within 5 business days; complete within 10 business days where practicable.

PA.name: Pennsylvania Right-to-Know Law
PA.note: Extendable by 30 calendar days with notice.

TX.name: Texas Public Information Act
TX.note: Produce promptly; if withholding, request an Attorney General ruling within 10 business days.

UT.name: Government Records Access and Management Act (GRAMA)

WI.name: Wisconsin Public Records Law
WI.note: As soon as practicable and without delay.

WY.name: Wyoming Public Records Act
WY.note: Records must be released within 30 calendar days of acknowledged receipt unless good cause exists (§ 16-4-202(b)(iii)); notices of unavailability are due within 7 business days (§ 16-4-202(b)).
